title: Royal charter granted to the East India Company
summary: Elizabeth I grants a charter giving the Company a monopoly on English trade east of the Cape of Good Hope.

title: Battle of Plassey
summary: Company forces under Robert Clive defeat the Nawab of Bengal, Siraj ud-Daulah, aided by defections arranged with Mir Jafar, who became Nawab.

title: Company receives the diwani of Bengal
summary: The Mughal emperor Shah Alam II grants the Company the right to collect revenue in Bengal, Bihar and Orissa.

title: Great Bengal famine
summary: Severe famine in Bengal under Company revenue administration. Mortality estimates are contested; contemporary figures of roughly a third of the population are debated by historians.

title: Regulating Act
summary: Parliament begins asserting oversight over the Company amid its financial crisis, creating a Governor-General of Bengal.

title: Company rule ends; Crown assumes control of India
summary: Following the 1857 rebellion, the Government of India Act transfers the Company's territories and armies to the Crown.

title: Iran nationalizes its oil industry
summary: Under Prime Minister Mohammad Mossadegh, Iran nationalizes the Anglo-Iranian Oil Company's holdings; Britain responds with an embargo and legal action.

title: Coup removes Mossadegh
summary: After an earlier failed attempt, a coup backed by the CIA and British MI6 removes Mossadegh and strengthens the rule of Shah Mohammad Reza Pahlavi.

title: Oil consortium agreement
summary: A multinational consortium, including British and US companies, takes over Iranian oil operations; Anglo-Iranian is renamed British Petroleum.

title: CIA publicly acknowledges its role
summary: Declassified CIA material released via the National Security Archive describes the 1953 operation as carried out under CIA direction.
